name: Madison Museum of Contemporary Art
funding: $2.9M expenses (2023); private donors and members; free admission.
watch: Ho-Chunk Gaming Madison, a casino, sponsors Art Fair on the Square. Separate 2022 Triennial racism row. Business Council list is not published.
why_flagged: Ho-Chunk Gaming Madison, a casino, sponsors Art Fair on the Square. Separate 2022 Triennial racism row. Business Council list is not published.
records_note: Its Form 990 is public for 2001 to 2025, it names Art Fair sponsors for 2025 and lists its trustees, but posts no annual reports.

name: Mansudae Art Museum / Mansudae Art Studio Gallery, 798
watch: Opened 2009 at 2 Jiuxianqiao Lu, north-west corner of 798, marked by a Chollima statue replica; sells originals, copies, posters and stamps. Taipei Times (Jan 2017) calls it Mansudae's 'only bricks and mortar foreign representation'; The Diplomat (Aug 2018) describes a 'Korea Traditional art center' in 798 operated by North Korea since c.2016. Koryo Tours' current guide says the 798 showing is 'closed' due to sanctions. Its director lent 13 works to the 2018 Gwangju Biennale for ₩28m.

records_note: No official website, report, accounts, funder list or board turned up for the state-run Mansudae studio gallery in Beijing, which is under international sanctions.

name: Mansudae Art Studio
funding: Directly financed by the Workers' Party of Korea and state treasury, augmented by overseas monument export revenues.
watch: Founded 17 Nov 1959; c.4,000 staff incl. c.700–1,000 artists; 120,000 m² complex. Exhibitions abroad: London 2007 and 2014, Brisbane 2009, Dandong 2013, Beijing 798 gallery from 2009. Kotra estimates North Korea earned over US$160m from art sales in the decade to 2018. Koryo Tours' guide says the studio 'is on the UN sanction list and cannot be visited nor art purchased'.

records_note: Its site, mansudaeartstudio.com, failed a secure connection, so no records could be checked.

name: Mansudae Overseas Project Group of Companies (Mansudae Overseas Projects)
watch: The UN listing covers all Mansudae operations and subsidiaries worldwide (Panel of Experts, 2017). Its US and EU listings are separate.
why_flagged: Builds monuments abroad, including the African Renaissance Monument in Dakar. Listed by the UN, US, EU and UK for exporting workers to raise revenue for the DPRK government.
records_note: A sanctioned North Korean overseas construction group; searches found only UN, UK and Australian sanctions listings, no website, report, accounts or board.

name: Mariupol Drama Theatre
funding: Rebuilt by Russian authorities and reopened on 28 December 2025 under the so-called Donetsk People's Republic, which the US, EU and UK list as a sanctioned entity.
watch: A Russian airstrike hit it on 16 March 2022 while civilians sheltered inside; AP counted close to 600 dead.
why_flagged: Rebuilt by Russian authorities and reopened on 28 December 2025 under the so-called Donetsk People's Republic, which the US, EU and UK list as a sanctioned entity.
records_note: The theatre was destroyed in March 2022 and reopened under Russian occupation; no official site, report, accounts, funder list or board turned up.

name: MASP
watch: Ultra fuel distributor and Bloomberg on roster.
why_flagged: Ultra fuel distributor and Bloomberg on roster.
records_note: MASP posts annual reports and financial statements for 2015 to 2024, fiscal council opinions, partner logos by tier without a date, and its full board.

name: MASS MoCA
funding: Massachusetts Cultural Council, Barr Foundation, NEA, admissions and individual philanthropy.
records_note: It posts no reports or accounts; ProPublica holds its Form 990s for 2001 to 2025, two funder logos sit in the footer, trustees are listed.

name: Mathaf: Arab Museum of Modern Art
watch: Funded by Qatar Museums, a Gulf state body under labour critique.
why_flagged: Funded by Qatar Museums, a Gulf state body under labour critique.
records_note: Mathaf has no records of its own; its parent Qatar Museums posts no reports, accounts or sponsor names but lists eight trustees.

name: Mauritshuis
records_note: It posts annual reports from 2013 to 2024, with financial reports for 2016 to 2018, names partners including NN Group, and names its supervisory board.

name: MAXXI
funding: Ministry of Culture EUR 14.0M in 2025, Regione Lazio 350k, Enel 600k as a promoter member, sponsors KME and Bulgari. Eni pays EUR 48,750 for archive work.
watch: On 27 October 2025 six artists withdrew and six collectives called a boycott over Eni, Leonardo and Gaza. MAXXI's 2025 accounts show no Leonardo money.
why_flagged: Ministry of Culture EUR 14.0M in 2025, Regione Lazio 350k, Enel 600k as a promoter member, sponsors KME and Bulgari. Eni pays EUR 48,750 for archive work.
records_note: It posts yearly accounts for 2020 to 2025 with a management report and names its board, but sponsors are undated logos.

name: Mémorial ACTe
funding: Public cultural body since 2019 joining the French state, Région Guadeloupe, the Département, Cap Excellence and Pointe-à-Pitre. The Région's then-president launched the €83M building.
watch: The regional audit court found serious irregularities in 2023. In April 2024 the financial prosecutor searched the Région's offices over the Mémorial's contracts.
why_flagged: The regional audit court found serious irregularities in 2023. In April 2024 the financial prosecutor searched the Région's offices over the Mémorial's contracts.
records_note: Its site carries ticketing, collections and administrative notices only; no annual reports, accounts, funder list or board are published.

name: Menil Collection
watch: Name to know: Bloomberg Philanthropies, top tier. 260+ UK artists asked five London theatres to drop it in May 2026; not targeted at the Menil.
why_flagged: Name to know: Bloomberg Philanthropies, top tier. 260+ UK artists asked five London theatres to drop it in May 2026; not targeted at the Menil.
records_note: Annual reports FY2013 to FY2025 and 990s are public; corporate sponsors are tiered logos, and the site has no board page.
